items.raw_excerpt: Scientists in the state of Vermont have spent the summer spreading Dutch elm disease to thousands of trees. It's an experiment to see if a new generation of elms might have resistance to a plague that has been decimating elm populations in the U.S. and Canada for decades.
items.summary_en: Scientists in Vermont spent the summer spreading Dutch elm disease to thousands of trees. The experiment aims to see if new elm trees can develop resistance to the disease. This could help protect elm populations across North America from further loss.
items.summary_ko: 버몬트주 과학자들이 올여름 수천 그루의 느릅나무에 네덜란드 올무병을 의도적으로 퍼뜨렸습니다. 이 실험은 새로운 세대의 나무들이 수십 년간 북미를 괴롭힌 이 질병에 대한 저항력을 가질 수 있는지 확인하기 위한 것입니다. 성공할 경우 북미 전역의 느릅나무 개체를 보호하는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.
items.title_en: Vermont Scientists Spread Dutch Elm Disease to Help Trees Fight Back

items.title_original: Dutch elm disease ravaged Canadian cities. Can we help trees protect themselves?

items.raw_excerpt: An easy hour's drive from Hobart, this regional town is chasing the capital city's title for Tassie's foodie hot spot.

items.raw_excerpt: Reportagem percorre territórios indígenas, reservas ambientais e centros de conservação para mostrar como espécies nativas resistem ao avanço urbano.
items.summary_en: A Brazilian TV program travels through indigenous lands, environmental reserves, and conservation centers to show how native species resist urban expansion. The report highlights the growing coexistence between city life and wild animals across Brazil. It aims to raise awareness about urban biodiversity and conservation efforts.
items.summary_ko: 브라질 TV 프로그램이 토착민 거주지, 환경 보호구역, 보존 센터를 돌아며 도시화 속에서도 살아남는 야생동물의 모습을 소개한다. 원주민 영역에서부터 도심까지 이어지는 자연과 도시의 공존을 다룬다. 도시 생태계 보전과 야생동물 보호에 대한 관심을 높이려는 취지로 제작됐다.

items.raw_excerpt: A hobbyist unearthed 4.5 kilos of Late Iron Age coins in Sysmä, marking the biggest find in Finland to date.
items.summary_en: A metal detector enthusiast found 4.5 kilos of Late Iron Age coins in Sysmä, Finland. This is the largest coin hoard ever discovered in the country. The find dates back to the Viking era.

items.raw_excerpt: French wine production this year is expected to fall 6 percent from 2025 after a summer of unprecedented heatwaves and drought, the agriculture ministry said on Monday, predicting the most paltry harvest for some 70 years.
items.summary_en: France expects wine production to fall 6 percent from 2025 after a summer of extreme heatwaves and drought. The agriculture ministry says this will be the smallest harvest in about 70 years. The hot and dry weather damaged vineyards across the country.
